label: HTML
description: Semantic markup, accessibility, forms, media and browser behaviour questions for web app development.

questions.title: What is the purpose of `<!DOCTYPE html>`?
questions.prompt: What is the purpose of `<!DOCTYPE html>`?

options.text: It imports the HTML5 specification into the page
It switches the browser into standards mode so CSS and layout follow the spec instead of legacy quirks
It declares the character encoding as UTF-8
It is required for JavaScript to run

questions.explanation: A missing or outdated doctype puts the browser into quirks mode, where box sizing and layout differ. Character encoding is declared separately with `<meta charset="utf-8">`.

questions.title: Why prefer `<nav>`, `<main>` and `<footer>` over a page of `<div>` elements?
questions.prompt: Why prefer `<nav>`, `<main>` and `<footer>` over a page of `<div>` elements?

options.text: Semantic elements render faster because the browser skips their layout
They convey document structure to browsers, assistive technology and search engines, and give screen-reader users landmarks to navigate by
Only semantic elements can contain text nodes
A `<div>` cannot be styled with CSS

questions.explanation: Landmark roles come for free from semantic elements, which improves keyboard navigation and SEO. Rendering speed is not the reason, and `<div>` is styleable like any other element.

questions.title: Which is the most accessible way to label a text input?
questions.prompt: Which is the most accessible way to label a text input?
questions.explanation: A programmatically associated `<label>` gives the input an accessible name, enlarges the click target and is announced by screen readers. Placeholder text disappears on input and is not a label substitute.

questions.title: What does adding `required` to an `<input>` do?
questions.prompt: What does adding `required` to an `<input>` do?

options.text: Nothing by itself — validation must be written in JavaScript
It enables constraint validation, so submitting an empty value blocks the submit and shows a validation message
It marks the field with a red border in every browser
It only affects how the field is rendered on mobile

questions.explanation: `required`, `type`, `pattern` and `min`/`max` participate in native constraint validation checked on submit, extensible through the Constraint Validation API.

questions.title: What is the difference between `<script defer>` and `<script async>`?
questions.prompt: What is the difference between `<script defer>` and `<script async>`?

options.text: Both download in parallel, but `defer` executes after parsing in document order while `async` executes as soon as it is downloaded
They are equivalent for external scripts

questions.explanation: Both attributes avoid render-blocking downloads. `defer` keeps execution order and runs before `DOMContentLoaded`, so it suits app bundles; `async` suits independent scripts such as analytics.

questions.title: A profile page is at `/users/7` and links to `href="edit"`. Where does it go?
questions.prompt: A profile page is at `/users/7` and links to `href="edit"`. Where does it go?

options.text: It depends on the `<base>` element; otherwise the request fails

questions.explanation: A relative URL resolves against the current document URL, so `edit` resolves to `/users/7/edit`. `/users/edit` would need `href="/users/edit"` or `href="../edit"`.

questions.title: Why does `alt` text matter on ``, and what belongs in it?
questions.prompt: Why does `alt` text matter on ``, and what belongs in it?

options.text: It is only used by search engines to rank the page
It is read by screen readers and shown if the image fails; it should describe the image's purpose, and decorative images should use `alt=""`
It is a tooltip shown on hover, so it should hold a caption
It is required only for PNG images

questions.explanation: `alt` is the accessible replacement for the image. Empty `alt` is the correct way to mark purely decorative images so screen readers skip them instead of reading a file name.

questions.title: Which attributes connect a data cell to its header in a complex table?
questions.prompt: Which attributes connect a data cell to its header in a complex table?

options.text: `headers` on `<td>` pointing at `id` attributes on the `<th>` cells it belongs to

questions.explanation: For multi-level headers, `<th id="...">` plus `<td headers="...">` associates cells with the right headers. `scope` on `<th>` handles simple tables, and `colspan`/`rowspan` only control layout.

questions.title: A single-page app serves the same `index.html` for every route. What is the consequence?
questions.prompt: A single-page app serves the same `index.html` for every route. What is the consequence?

options.text: None — crawlers execute JavaScript exactly like users
Every route shares one title and description unless the document head is updated per route (or content is pre-rendered/server-rendered), which hurts SEO and link previews
The browser caches the wrong route

questions.explanation: Crawler support for client rendering is inconsistent. Per-route metadata (Next.js `metadata`/`generateMetadata`, or prerendering) gives each URL its own title, description and social preview.

questions.title: Which input type is the right choice for a quantity between 1 and 10 that must be keyboard-friendly?
questions.prompt: Which input type is the right choice for a quantity between 1 and 10 that must be keyboard-friendly?
questions.explanation: `type="number"` keeps typing and arrow-key stepping, participates in `min`/`max` validation and still shows a numeric keypad via `inputmode`. A range slider is poor for precise entry and a select adds unnecessary interaction.

questions.title: Which element must be the direct child of `<html>`?
questions.prompt: Which element must be the direct child of `<html>`?
questions.explanation: The document element `<html>` contains exactly two children: `<head>` (metadata) and `<body>` (visible content).

questions.title: What is the main benefit of using `<main>` over a `<div>`?
questions.prompt: What is the main benefit of using `<main>` over a `<div>`?

options.text: It gives screen readers and browser tools a landmark for the page's primary content
It makes HTML valid only when required

questions.explanation: Landmarks such as `<main>`, `<nav>` and `<aside>` let assistive technology jump between page regions; a div gives no such meaning.

questions.title: What does the `alt` attribute provide for an image?
questions.prompt: What does the `alt` attribute provide for an image?

options.text: A text alternative read aloud when the image cannot be displayed

questions.explanation: alt text is both the fallback when the image fails to load and what screen readers announce.

questions.title: Which input type gives mobile users a numeric keypad?
questions.prompt: Which input type gives mobile users a numeric keypad?
questions.explanation: type="number" (and type="tel"/type="numeric" variants) signals a numeric entry, prompting the on-screen numeric keypad.

questions.title: What does the `controls` attribute on `<video>` do?
questions.prompt: What does the `controls` attribute on `<video>` do?

options.text: Displays the browser's default play/pause/seek controls

questions.explanation: Without `controls` the player has no UI; the attribute is the standard way to expose the native control bar.

questions.title: Which attribute opens a link in a new tab?
questions.prompt: Which attribute opens a link in a new tab?
questions.explanation: `target="_blank"` requests a new browsing context; pair it with `rel="noopener"` for safety.

questions.title: Which element contains the actual data cells of a table?
questions.prompt: Which element contains the actual data cells of a table?
questions.explanation: `<thead>`/`<tfoot>` hold header/footer rows; `<tbody>` groups the body rows (and is often added automatically by the parser).

questions.title: What is the correct heading hierarchy for a page?
questions.prompt: What is the correct heading hierarchy for a page?

options.text: Any order, as long as they are large
One h1 for the page title, then headings without skipping levels as sections nest
Headings must go in reverse order

questions.explanation: A single h1 per page (its main topic) with sequential h2/h3… levels lets screen readers reconstruct the outline.

questions.title: Where does `<title>` belong?
questions.prompt: Where does `<title>` belong?
questions.explanation: `<title>` is document metadata, so it lives in `<head>`; the browser shows it in the tab and it is required for valid HTML5.

questions.title: What does a `label` element's `for` attribute do?
questions.prompt: What does a `label` element's `for` attribute do?

options.text: Associates the label with an input so clicking the text focuses the control and screen readers announce it

questions.explanation: The `for`/`id` pairing makes the whole label clickable and binds the accessible name to the control.

questions.title: What is the difference between `defer` and `async` on a `<script>` tag?
questions.prompt: What is the difference between `defer` and `async` on a `<script>` tag?

options.text: defer blocks parsing, async does not
Both are fetched in parallel — defer runs after parsing in order, async runs as soon as it's ready (possibly mid-parse, out of order)
async blocks parsing, defer does not

questions.explanation: defer preserves order and waits for the DOM; async scripts execute the moment they load, so order and DOM readiness are both lost.

questions.title: Which attribute makes a form field required before submit?
questions.prompt: Which attribute makes a form field required before submit?
questions.explanation: The `required` attribute triggers the browser's native validation; `novalidate` on the form is what *disables* validation.

questions.title: When should `<article>` be preferred over `<section>`?
questions.prompt: When should `<article>` be preferred over `<section>`?

options.text: When the content makes sense as a standalone, distributable unit (a post, a card) without needing the surrounding context

questions.explanation: `<article>` marks self-contained content; `<section>` groups thematically related content that normally needs a heading.

questions.title: How do you make a cell span two columns?
questions.prompt: How do you make a cell span two columns?
questions.explanation: `colspan` spans columns (and `rowspan` spans rows) on `<th>`/`<td>`.

questions.title: What does `rel="noopener"` protect against on external links?
questions.prompt: What does `rel="noopener"` protect against on external links?

options.text: The opened page using `window.opener` to navigate your tab (reverse tabnabbing)

questions.explanation: Without noopener, the new tab receives `window.opener` and can replace your page with a phishing lookalike. Modern browsers default to noopener, but the attribute documents intent.

questions.title: Which meta tag controls how a page appears in search results?
questions.prompt: Which meta tag controls how a page appears in search results?
questions.explanation: The description meta is the usual source of the snippet text under a result; the others affect encoding, policy and mobile layout.

questions.title: A linked image repeats the link's visible text in its alt attribute. Why is that a problem?
questions.prompt: A linked image repeats the link's visible text in its alt attribute. Why is that a problem?

options.text: The alt text becomes part of the link's accessible name — if it repeats the link text, the announcement becomes verbose

questions.explanation: Screen readers announce link names as a whole; alt text that duplicates surrounding words creates noisy 'click here' style links.

questions.title: What does `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` achieve?
questions.prompt: What does `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` achieve?

options.text: Sets the page's pixel width only
Makes the layout viewport match the device width at 1× zoom — the foundation of mobile-friendly pages

questions.explanation: Without this tag mobile browsers lay out at a ~980px viewport and shrink it; adding it enables responsive CSS to work as designed.

questions.title: Why is `<input type="email">` better than `type="text"` for an email field?
questions.prompt: Why is `<input type="email">` better than `type="text"` for an email field?

options.text: It performs built-in client-side format validation and, on mobile, presents an appropriate keyboard

questions.explanation: The email type gives free browser validation and tailored keyboards; real submission checks still belong on the server.

questions.title: What is the purpose of `<track kind="subtitles">` inside `<video>`?
questions.prompt: What is the purpose of `<track kind="subtitles">` inside `<video>`?

options.text: Provides timed text tracks for captions/subtitles/cues that the player renders

questions.explanation: The `<track>` element supplies WebVTT cues; kind selects captions, subtitles, descriptions, chapters or metadata.

questions.title: Why can `defer` still delay the first paint on a page?
questions.prompt: Why can `defer` still delay the first paint on a page?

options.text: The browser must finish fetching all defer scripts before DOMContentLoaded — a slow third-party defer script stalls interactive time

questions.explanation: defer scripts run in order right after parsing; a large or slow file keeps the main thread waiting, which shows up as a long TTI.

questions.title: Where does an inline `<script>` without async/defer execute?
questions.prompt: Where does an inline `<script>` without async/defer execute?

options.text: Immediately where it appears, pausing HTML parsing at that point

questions.explanation: Classic inline scripts block parsing — inline code can only reach elements parsed *before* it, which is why scripts usually sit at the end or defer.

questions.title: What is the practical difference between `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby`?
questions.prompt: What is the practical difference between `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby`?

options.text: aria-label supplies the accessible name inline; aria-labelledby points at another element's id whose text becomes the name

questions.explanation: labelledby is used when the name already exists visibly elsewhere on the page, keeping the two in sync; aria-label writes it directly.

questions.title: Why does `novalidate` on a form sometimes get added with JS validation?
questions.prompt: Why does `novalidate` on a form sometimes get added with JS validation?

options.text: To suppress the browser's built-in popup so a custom, consistent error UI can be shown instead

questions.explanation: novalidate takes over validation from the browser — the form's JS must then enforce (and communicate) the same rules itself.

questions.title: Why is `<button>` preferable to a clickable `<div>`?
questions.prompt: Why is `<button>` preferable to a clickable `<div>`?

options.text: It is focusable, activatable by keyboard/screen readers, and carries button semantics natively

questions.explanation: A div needs JavaScript, tabIndex, key handlers and ARIA just to reach parity — the native button already has all of it.

questions.title: What problem does `loading="lazy"` on an `` solve — and what does it change?
questions.prompt: What problem does `loading="lazy"` on an `` solve — and what does it change?

options.text: It defers off-screen images until near the viewport, changing when (not whether) they load and their measured load events
It removes the image from the accessibility tree

questions.explanation: Lazy loading cuts initial bandwidth but can push image downloads past first paint and after LCP, hurting the metric it was meant to help.

questions.title: Why is a `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` on a staging page often missed?
questions.prompt: Why is a `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` on a staging page often missed?

options.text: Crawlers must be able to fetch the page to read the meta tag — blocked robots.txt prevents noindex from ever being seen
It must be in the head of the sitemap

questions.explanation: Noindex is evaluated during a crawl. If robots.txt disallows fetching, the directive never arrives and the page can still be indexed from external links.

questions.title: What happens when `<main>` appears twice on one page?
questions.prompt: What happens when `<main>` appears twice on one page?

options.text: It is invalid — only one visible non-hidden `<main>` is allowed per document

questions.explanation: Landmarks must be unique; two mains make 'jump to main' ambiguous for assistive technology.

questions.title: Why does `<video autoplay>` often fail without `muted`?
questions.prompt: Why does `<video autoplay>` often fail without `muted`?

options.text: Browser policies block unmuted autoplay; muted autoplay is the allowed escape hatch
The video file must be muted

questions.explanation: To protect users from surprise audio, Chrome and friends reject autoplaying audio — keeping the media muted lets the video start.

questions.title: What does `<table><caption>` provide that a heading above the table does not?
questions.prompt: What does `<table><caption>` provide that a heading above the table does not?

options.text: An accessible table title that screen readers announce with the table itself

questions.explanation: caption is programmatically associated with the table, so assistive tech reads it as the table's name when navigating.
